answer_1.quote: To address the vacuous responses problem in neural dialog models, researchers propose to ground dialogs on real world knowledge...

answer_2.quote: For automatic evaluation, we evaluate the generated responses from three perspectives : • Appropriateness: we employ Perplexity (PPL), corpus-level  and ROUGE-l . • Diversity: the ratio of distinct uni/bi-grams in all generated texts, i.e., Distinct-1/2 . • Informativeness: For WoW, we consider wikiF1 , the overlapping F1 between the generated response and the grounded knowledge. For CRD, we calculate entity score (Ent.) , the average number of entities per response.

answer_4.quote: We further perform human annotations by randomly sampling 200/200/300/300 examples from WoW Test Seen/WoW Test Unseen/ CRD/DailyDialog, respectively. We recruit 5 annotators from a commercial annotation company to rate each response on a scale of 1-5 for its appropriateness  and informativeness .
answer_4.guideline: The former measures whether the topic of the response fits that of the utterance, while the latter evaluates whether a response provides new information. A response is scored 1 if it is not appropriate/informative at all, 3 if part of the response is appropriate/informative, 5 if it is highly related to utterance and context or it can provide rich information to deepen the discussion. 2 and 4 are for decision dilemmas.
